document.abstract: The introduction of the recordable laser videodisc has brought the full process of videodisc technology into the user's hands. Along with the playback power of fast access on low-cost players, the user can now record the disc in his own facility in real time. The burden of properly formatting and encoding the material for disc is now in-house. The Laser Vision videodisc and an encoder/generator that encodes the vertical interval to the IEC specifications in the Laser Vision standard are described.
